article_title: Assessment of understanding, attitudes, and clinical practices regarding osteoporosis among postgraduate students in China.
citation: Ding Hong, Li He-Xi, Ai You-Wei, Zhang Qing-Yi, Tang Hai-Tao, Zeng Wen. (2025). Assessment of understanding, attitudes, and clinical practices regarding osteoporosis among postgraduate students in China. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-07785-5
title: 14-item structured osteoporosis knowledge, awareness, and practice questionnaire
description: A structured 14-item questionnaire in three sections assessing osteoporosis knowledge (five questions), awareness and learning level (six questions), and clinical practice (three questions). It was developed from Chinese diagnosis and treatment guidelines with design principles from the "Osteoporosis in Older Men: Knowledge and Health Beliefs" questionnaire, reviewed by three osteoporosis specialists, and pilot-tested with "satisfactory internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.78)". It was distributed electronically via WeChat and Questionnaire Star to 97 postgraduates.
requirements: Specialist review of clinical relevance, clarity, and comprehensiveness and pilot testing before implementation
constraints: Developed for and administered to postgraduates at one Chinese institution; anonymous voluntary completion
target_learning_goals: osteoporosis knowledge, awareness, and clinical practice self-report
examples: Sample items include "What is the definition of osteoporosis?" and "How frequently do you offer advice to older patients about preventing osteoporosis?"
